verdict.rationale: Ramp offers a broad programmatic surface: a Developer API with 174 documented OpenAPI paths, an agent-oriented CLI covering 12 resources (bills, cards, transactions, reimbursements, travel, and more), an OAuth-gated MCP server with dozens of read/write scopes, and end-to-end bill payment via the API. However, Ramp never claims full UI parity, and its own docs show UI-only gaps: bill approvals are not available via MCP and are routed to the UI or a separate API, partner applications must be finished 'in the Ramp UI', and incorporation is private-preview only. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement or coverage map, API coverage of every UI workflow (e.g. applicant sign-up completion), general availability of gated endpoints, and independent hands-on corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: a parseable OpenAPI document titled "Ramp Developer API" (v1) with 174 documented paths
Authenticate with OAuth, manage expenses, approve bills, book travel, and more — from your terminal or AI agent.
Create approved bills via the API, attach documents, choose a payment method, and pay vendors end-to-end
Approve or reject transactions, reimbursements, and unified requests (purchase orders, fund requests, procurement approvals)
